Playbook.name: Kaspersky — Multiple Threat Detections on One Endpoint - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: Kaspersky reported multiple distinct threat detections on one endpoint in the window (ES|QL aggregate) - a pattern of active compromise rather than a single caught object. Triage: an actively-compromised endpoint, or repeated detections of one benign-flagged item?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Multiple threats on one endpoint indicates an active infection dropping/executing several malicious objects.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Kaspersky Security Center CEF (verified live). Fields: destination.domain (the affected ENDPOINT, not the collector), destination.user.name, cef.device.event_class_id, cef.name, message (malware name/path/SHA256), source.ip. Use destination.domain as the host of interest.

Signal.Name: Multiple Threat Detections on One Endpoi
Signal.Details: endpoint with multiple distinct Kaspersky threat detections.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the endpoint is actively compromised (multiple real threats) or repeatedly flagging one benign item.

Step.name: Distinct threats on the endpoint
Step.Purpose: The variety and names of threats distinguish active compromise from one repeated false-positive.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND cef.device.event_class_id RLIKE "(?i).*(virus|object_blocked|notcured|attack|adsec).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS detections = COUNT(*), distinct_threats = COUNT_DISTINCT(cef.name), threats = VALUES(cef.name), classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Several DISTINCT threat names/classes = active compromise (multiple payloads). Many detections of ONE name = a single item repeatedly flagged (possibly benign or a persistent uncured object).

Step.name: Disposition - was any threat uncured/active
Step.Purpose: Uncured/blocked-but-recurring threats among the set confirm active infection.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE cef.device.vendor == "KasperskyLab" AND destination.domain == "$endpoint" AND cef.device.event_class_id RLIKE "(?i).*notcured.*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS uncured = COUNT(*), names = VALUES(cef.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Any uncured threat among multiple detections = active infection - isolate.

Node.Condition: Multiple distinct real threats, or any uncured threat, on the endpoint.
Many detections of a single benign-flagged item (all cured).
A test/EICAR or security-exercise generating multiple benign detections.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-KASMULTI-THREATS, INV-02-KASMULTI-DISPOSITION to the case.

TruePositive.Definition: An actively-compromised endpoint with multiple payloads.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the endpoint; full IR; hunt the payloads/hashes across the estate.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the affected endpoint (destination.domain) and the threat.
If malware active/uncured or spreading, isolate the endpoint.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the endpoint; run a full scan; capture the sample; open IR.
Hunt the same malware/hash across endpoints.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Ensure Kaspersky is enforcing + updated; add the hash/IOC to blocklists; verify EDR coverage.

QualityChecks.Check: Kaspersky reports the endpoint in destination.domain (host.* is the collector pod) - always pivot on destination.domain.
The CEF pipeline occasionally mislabels events - see the pipeline health note in the phase-1 report.
